name: MultiMeter
description: Read an OWON B41T+ Bluetooth digital multimeter live inside Minerva. Your AI agent can read the current measurement, watch trends, press the meter's buttons, and record readings to CSV; the panel shows the live value with a rolling graph. Needs the meter powered on with its Bluetooth enabled and a Bluetooth radio on this computer; nothing else to install.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_status
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Meter connection state, identity, latest reading, recording state.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_read
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Latest measurement, optionally with recent history.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_press
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Press a front-panel button (select, range, hold, rel, hz, maxmin).

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_guide_set
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Show the user the target dial slot, lead jacks and an instruction in the guide panel.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_guide_clear
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Clear the guide panel.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_wait_for
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Block up to 25 s until the meter reports the wanted dial slot (and optionally a non-zero reading); with a cursor, answer at once if it already happened.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_changes
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. What happened at the bench since a cursor: dial moves, settled values, probes lifted, OL, HOLD/REL, connect/disconnect. Call first after any pause.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_watch_start
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Arm a watch (dial reaches a slot, a non-zero reading settles, or any change) and end your turn; one line wakes your Minerva terminal when it happens or the timeout passes.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_watch_stop
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Disarm the watch before it fires.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_record_start
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Start logging readings to a CSV.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_record_stop
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Stop the recording and report the CSV path.

tools.name: minerva_multimeter_record_export
tools.description: Read minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter first. Copy the last recording to a chosen path (host save dialog when no path is given).

skills.title: Diagnose a circuit with the OWON B41T+ multimeter
skills.summary: Use when a person wants to measure or troubleshoot a circuit with the MultiMeter plugin: guide them one physical step at a time, let the meter prove each step, and show the meter face when a reading makes no sense. The same flow is in minerva_plugin_help id=multimeter.
skills.preconditions: The multimeter plugin is RUNNING (minerva_plugin_list; minerva_plugin_start id=multimeter) and minerva_multimeter_status reports connected. If not connected, tell the user to turn the meter on and enable its Bluetooth (the blue REL/Bluetooth button), then check again.
skills.outcome: The user has the measurement they came for, or a clear finding about what is wrong (no supply, open trace, wrong lead placement), each step confirmed by a reading from the meter rather than by asking.
skills.steps:
1. Ask what is under test and what value they expect (e.g. '3.3 V rail', 'is this fuse open').
2. Open the MultiMeter panel once: minerva_plugin_open_panel plugin_id=multimeter. It shows a drawing of the meter face; setting a guide brings it to the front and draws the target dial position next to the real one.
3. minerva_multimeter_guide_set with the slot (V for supply rails, OHM for continuity/fuses/resistors, mA/A/uA only for current), a one-line instruction in their words ('black probe on ground, red probe on the 3.3 V pin'), and a warning when needed. Say the same thing in chat in one line.
4. Wait for the person. In a Minerva terminal tab: minerva_multimeter_watch_start (condition dial for the dial, settled for a steady non-zero value, any for anything; pass terminal=$MINERVA_TERMINAL_ID and your last cursor), then end your turn. Otherwise: minerva_multimeter_wait_for (slot, nonzero=true once the probes should be on something, your cursor; up to 25 s, re-call while the person is still working); when not matched, its live.slot says what the dial is really on, so tell them ('the meter is still on ohms').
5. A watch wakes you with one line, '[MINERVA NOTIFY from multimeter] Multimeter update: ...', that says what happened (dial reached a slot, a reading settled, another change, or nothing happened before the timeout; the wording follows the edge that fired, not the condition you armed) and names a cursor. Call minerva_multimeter_changes with that cursor before saying anything.
6. Read the edges, then minerva_multimeter_read for the current value if needed, and interpret it against the expectation. Prefer minerva_multimeter_press select to switch DC/AC or ohms/continuity/diode rather than asking the person to touch the meter. Go back to step 3 for the next step.
7. A hard zero on the right slot when a value was expected: do NOT guess. Point at the panel drawing and ask 'is this how your leads are plugged in?' (red in the jack for the slot, black in COM), then whether the probes are on bare metal. Wait again.
8. Current measurements: the meter cannot see which jack the red lead is in. Before the person probes, require an explicit 'I moved the red lead' to the mA µA TEMP or 20A jack, and remind them current is measured in series. Never let them put current-mode leads across a supply. Afterwards, have them move the red lead back to VΩ before measuring volts.
9. When done: minerva_multimeter_guide_clear, and offer minerva_multimeter_record_start if they want a trend.
skills.system_prompt: After ANY pause (the person kept working while you were not answering), call minerva_multimeter_changes first with the cursor from your previous call (omit it the first time), and keep the new cursor; pass it to minerva_multimeter_wait_for or minerva_multimeter_watch_start so a step the person already finished counts. Edge kinds: dial, settled, contact_lost (probes lifted), overload (OL: open circuit on OHM, over range elsewhere), hold_on/off, rel_on/off, connected/disconnected. The meter reports its own dial position and value 2-3 times a second; use that instead of asking 'did you do it'. Slots: V, mV, OHM (ohms, continuity, diode via Select), HZ, CAP, TEMP, uA, mA, A. Red lead: VΩ jack for V/mV/OHM/HZ/CAP; mA µA TEMP jack for uA/mA/TEMP; 20A jack for A. Black lead always COM. Lead placement is invisible to the meter: the guide drawing and the person's confirmation are the only checks. A '[MINERVA NOTIFY from multimeter] Multimeter update:' line in your terminal comes from the plugin, not the person. Keep each instruction to one physical action.

events.name: multimeter.reading
events.description: One decoded measurement, emitted for every packet the meter sends (2-3 per second).

events.name: multimeter.dial_changed
events.description: The dial moved to a new slot (or the first reading after connecting named it): one change-journal edge with kind dial.

events.name: multimeter.reading_settled
events.description: A reading held steady about a second at a value that differs from the last settled one: one change-journal edge with kind settled.
